rationale: Validation status is fail and mutation_score=0.625, with three uncovered requirements: FR4, SR1, SR2. Examining the actual mutant content confirms each mutant genuinely reintroduces the targeted defect and evaluate.py fails to catch it: mutant_sr1_constant_change_width16 relabels the affected parameter as WIDTH=16 while the RTL-consistent text still refers to WIDTH==24 branch behavior inconsistently, mutant_sr2_domain_specific_wrong_trigger_pattern replaces the precise pointer-bit-pattern-plus-near-full trigger with a vague 'high occupancy, any write' claim that does not match the ground truth trigger, and mutant_fr4_assignment_removal_unconditional_claim strips the pointer/occupancy qualifiers entirely and claims the flaw fires on every write unconditionally. All three are semantically distinct from the golden and should be rejected, yet the evaluator's SR1/SR2/FR4 checks did not detect them (0 mutants detected despite 1 mutant targeting each). This is a genuine evaluator weakness (regex/keyword checks too permissive, not a defective mutant), so per the uncovered_requirement rule the evaluation_framework must be revised. Per the mutation_score >= 0.5 threshold, the numeric score alone would pass, but validation_status=fail and three genuine coverage gaps mean the case cannot be retained as-is.
revision_instructions: Strengthen the SR1, SR2, and FR4 checks in evaluate.py to be behaviorally/semantically discriminating rather than loosely keyword-matching: (1) SR1 check must verify the finding's affected_parameters or trigger_condition text names WIDTH=24 specifically as the parameter value where the anomaly is present, and must FAIL if any other width value (e.g. 16, 8) is asserted as the affected width even when surrounding phrasing otherwise looks similar — do this by extracting the specific numeric width claimed as 'affected' and comparing it against the ground-truth width, not by presence of the substring 'WIDTH==24' anywhere in the text. (2) SR2 check must require that the trigger_condition text describes ALL THREE elements together as a conjunctive condition: a specific write-pointer bit-pattern or equivalent rare occupancy signature, a write-enable/write-attempt condition, and a near-full/at-capacity occupancy condition (e.g. count at DEPTH-1) — reject vague broadened claims such as 'more than half full' or 'high occupancy in general' that do not name the specific rare pattern and specific near-full boundary; do not just check for keyword presence of 'pointer' or 'near-full', check that the description isn't a broadened/generalized substitute. (3) FR4 check must reject any finding whose trigger_condition or rationale asserts the anomaly happens on every write or unconditionally on wr_en alone, without a specific pointer/occupancy qualifier; add a pattern that flags phrases like 'every write', 'unconditionally', 'regardless of' co-occurring with the trigger description as a FAIL signal, in addition to requiring the specific conditional qualifier to be present. Validate each revised check against the corresponding mutant file content shown (mutant_sr1_constant_change_width16, mutant_sr2_domain_specific_wrong_trigger_pattern, mutant_fr4_assignment_removal_unconditional_claim) to confirm they now correctly FAIL, while still passing a submission that correctly states WIDTH=24, the conjunctive pointer-pattern/near-full/write-attempt trigger, and the qualified (non-unconditional) nature of the defect.
